# DKR-023: No host network, PID or IPC namespace

- **Group:** Docker
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

With the host PID namespace a container sees and can signal every host process; as root it can read their memory and environment. With the host network it binds directly on the host, bypasses Docker's network isolation and reaches every loopback service; as root it can also change the host's network. The host IPC namespace shares memory segments with host processes. A container that is not running (a one shot init container that exited, or a stopped one) is reported as info, since the setting matters only when it starts. The platform's own containers (Coolify's panel stack, coolify-proxy and coolify-sentinel; Dokploy's panel, database, Redis and Traefik) keep their findings at most at warn while the platform is detected, marked as managed by the platform, because the panel does not let you change them; privileged stays a fail.

## Verify by hand

```sh
docker inspect --format '{{.Name}} net={{.HostConfig.NetworkMode}} pid={{.HostConfig.PidMode}} ipc={{.HostConfig.IpcMode}}' $(docker ps -aq)
```

## How to fix it

Use a bridge network and publish only the ports needed (on 127.0.0.1 behind the proxy); remove pid: host and ipc: host.

## What a fix can break

Tools that monitor host processes or need host networking (some VPNs, node exporters) need another setup.

Run `stackward explain DKR-023` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
